sources.entry: Reactotron - Desktop app for inspecting your React JS and React Native projects. macOS, Linux, and Windows.

summary.one_liner: Reactotron is a desktop debugger for React and React Native apps that shows application state, network requests, logs, and performance metrics.
summary.what_it_does: Reactotron is a debugging tool that runs as a desktop app and connects to a React or React Native project through a dev dependency. The README describes it as able to view application state, show API requests and responses, run quick performance benchmarks, and display messages similar to console.log. It can track global errors with source-mapped stack traces, including saga stack traces. It also supports dispatching actions and hot swapping app state using Redux or mobx-state-tree. For React Native, the README lists image overlays and Async Storage tracking. Desktop builds are published on the Releases page for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
use_cases: track global errors with stack traces
view Async Storage contents in React Native
how_to_run: On the Releases page, download the latest reactotron-app release for your platform
Install Reactotron as a dev dependency in your React or React Native project
Follow the README setup guides for React Native or React
Enable the desired plugins (Networking, Redux, Async Storage, Benchmark, etc.)
notable: Plugs in as a dev dependency so it adds nothing to production builds
Source-mapped global error tracking, including saga stack traces
Hot swap app state with Redux or mobx-state-tree
Storybook switching from the desktop app (React Native only)
Open-source and free, built by Infinite Red
caveats: Setup requires installing the desktop app and adding client libraries to the project
Storybook integration is only for React Native per the README
README does not describe licensing details beyond the open-source statement
